40小时全成就，售价不值。弹珠肉鸽，很新颖的打法，明明有更好的呈现方式，偏偏选择了最无聊的挂机资源放置和无限升级。 先讲优点： 1.弹珠+肉鸽，目前无竞品，想法很新颖，能给新玩家全新的体验。 2.前期开荒（大概前15小时）很爽，很上瘾，每一把尝试新的合成和弹珠，游玩时还要注意弹射轨道，即使反馈很强。 缺点也难以接受： 1.前期局外成长特别慢，可能打好几把才能收获一点点局外成长，局外成长设计成建筑经营，比较有想法，但体验着实不好。 2.中期如果想快速局外成长，需要去关关卡里面自杀、到局外刷金币，重复这个过程很多次，否则会成长得特别慢。 3.后期几乎沦为数值游戏，只要数值上去了，瞎玩，瞎选技能都能赢。 4.大后期的局外成长更是使中使，开通了一个无限升级的功能，对游戏中的几个关键属性给了局外成长无限升级。从此以后基本就无聊得没法玩了。 5.对于全通过的后续流程设计，更是烂的一坨。市面上这么多游戏给了这么多例子，很多肉鸽游戏都有无尽模式，不知道为什么你们抄都抄不明白。该游戏全通之后，就是新的一轮一模一样的关卡，只是该轮关卡中怪物的数值被加强。因此为了通关，又需要刷局外成长的无限升级。形成了“关卡数值无限上升”+“角色数值无限升级”的套娃式循坏。至于局内的弹珠、物品、研究厉害的合成路径和打法，统统不重要。无聊至极。 个人认为后期比较好的游戏方式：取消无限升级，取消关卡无限套娃，开通无尽模式。局内游戏中，选择让玩家能够更加自由地选择想要的道具，有更多刷新道具和选择道具的机会，尽早形成自己的道具搭配，在无尽模式中尝试研究更厉害的道具搭配，刷无尽模式。
我已经能想象到几个月后，这个游戏被国内某厂做成手游，登上畅销榜的画面了；
当你打过关卡后如果点击<重试>会吞掉你本次过关的收益！！！！！！必须点击<返回基地> 这应该是一个BUG，如果是设计，那这是一个不恰当的错误，希望能快些修复！！ 游戏很好玩！

游戏模式还行，但是局内成长的bd太少基本公式化，纯靠局外成长的数值耗时间，而且数值给得非常抠搜。有点白瞎这个打弹珠的玩法框架了。初玩的半个小时还是有爽感的。第一关打半天发现数值直接给你卡死，在肝到很后期的局外成长之前甚至根本没法过难度3。打折40多块rmb我觉得还是贵了。总地来说，刚靠设定吸引你一下然后就进入到很快餐的无聊阶段，要不停地肝然后才能在很久之后接触到一些剩余的不多的内容 深度游玩之后补充： 前面的评价不需要作出任何改变。并且，我举个例子说明一下让人很难绷的局面。 这游戏的设定是两个升满级的武器可以进行融合，从而让特效互相叠加。这看似能够组建出很多bd——但是实际上的情况是，当我进化出一个能够全屏攻击的武器（灯泡）并且将其升满，然后将它和另一个同样等级的流血武器（蚊子还是什么，名字忘了）进行融合之后，“全屏攻击+分裂流血”的特效并没有出现，后者的特性直接等同消失不见了。而由于这种愚蠢的无效组合（大量存在），我这一局就gg了。问题在于，这符合一般的若割游戏的逻辑吗？哪怕不能变强，这种技能融合直接变一坨的意图是什么呢？出于没有背板那些制作者设想的寥寥几个强力组合？ 这背后的逻辑显然是：做游戏的人并没有考虑到这种所谓的融合机制的深度内容，他们大概做了几个有限的组合之后就觉得差不多了——玩家不需要进行这些固定搭配之外的自行探索。也就是说，这游戏虽然看似是组建bd的，其实根本就不是——它的所谓“随机要素”就是单纯的敷衍和诱骗。 很难想象大量好评是怎么出现的——看来制作者对玩家的想象既是轻蔑的，又是准确的。

BALL x PIT is a fascinatingly fun game, perfect for blowing off some steam after a rough day. Obliterating enemies has never been so much fun! The way you can uniquely upgrade and synergize your balls on each run makes for some really creative builds. Each level offers enough variation to provide endless combinations of playthrough strategies. The soundtrack is awesome and adds an even more unique flavor to this already delicious game. I especially love how each level has its own individual remix of the first level's song and how it matches the theme/biome of each level. The ending animation you are awarded with for the "true ending" is beautiful, hypnotic, and a sight to behold. Only 25% of players have witnessed that animation. We need to pump those numbers up! Highly recommended!

I don’t dislike the Bullet Heaven genre. It’s never been a system built primarily around skill so much as knowledge. You pick up items and abilities that optimize synergy, giving your run the best chance of success. There is something immensely satisfying about watching the numbers climb as everything dies around you like insects. The genre’s main issue is that every game struggles to feel distinct from the last. Each new entry is trying desperatly to find a way to stand out in a "I swear we're not completely like Vampire Survivors" kind of way. That’s not a problem if you simply want more of the same, but it does mean that if you’re craving something genuinely different within the genre, you have to search a little harder. Ball X Pit does, in fact, do a fantastic job of standing apart. Throw an auto-scroller, bullet hell, bullet heaven, and pinball into a blender and somehow it creates something weird, wonderful, and genuinely fresh. Instead of selecting traditional weapons, you choose balls (go figure) and fire them into the arena, where they bounce around triggering all sorts of effects. Some pass through enemies, some create area-of-effect explosions, some spawn additional balls, and others provide crowd control. Like many games in the genre, knowledge remains key. You still have to think about what combinations work best and which balls synergize, but now positioning and aim matter just as much. The strongest synergies in the world won’t help if you can’t land your shots for optimal bounces. It's a bullet heaven actually demands some degree of skill, and that’s more than I can say for most titles in this space. Layered on top of that is your choice of character, and later, multiple characters at once. They don’t just change your starting ball; they fundamentally alter how the game plays. Some are lame, leaning into the “plays itself” kind of design, but most introduce radical new approaches. One makes the game turn-based, another makes balls return to you, one fires from the back of the screen, one skips basic shots entirely in favor of stacking powerful buffs. Once you unlock the ability to bring two characters together, the game transforms into a chaotic mix of skill, strategy, and wild experimentation as you chase ridiculous, overpowered combos. It all adds up to something genuinely unique in a genre that often struggles with identity. Does it have problems? Sure. It doesn’t escape the slide into passivity once you become truly powerful. Even in New Game+ you’ll eventually get so broken that the skill requirement largely evaporates. There’s a manual firing option for your balls… which is mostly useless. I’m only half-joking; one or two characters benefit from deliberate shots, but for the vast majority, raw output beats precision. The home base you return to between runs for upgrades is also a bit tedious. You place structures and resources to build and collect, but you’ll constantly need to rearrange everything to fit new buildings or upgrade existing ones. It can feel like it’s pulling you away from the part you actually want to do: jumping back into the next run. Still, these are minor complaints. For what Ball X Pit sets out to do, it delivers exactly the satisfying, high-energy experience it promises. If you’re looking for something in the genre that’s more than just a little different, this one absolutely delivers. Fully recommended.

If you're looking for a brick-breaking roguelike with light city building mechanics, you're in the right place. There's tons of combinations, evolutions, fusions, accessories, characters, balls, enemies, bosses, stages, difficulties, and even new game plus. The sheer amount of content and competent gameplay mechanics makes this worth playing if the gameplay appeals to you. Even after completing all the achievements I haven't done everything there is to do in the game. That being said, if you just want to clear the game and enjoy the ride it might take around 15-20 hours. Overall, pretty fun game.

[h1]它也许不是一款优秀的肉鸽，但一定是一款优秀的电子阳痿特效药。[/h1] 这是一款完全不需要操作，也几乎不需要思考的纯粹的爽游，可以理解为类吸血鬼幸存者的另一种形式。其核心的爽感来源是各种不一样的球在有限的空间里不断弹射并在怪物身上爆出数字，以及场外收集和整理建筑的微量养成元素。游戏里的不同角色平衡性做得并不算好但也算各有特色，玩法和球的设计却是非常无脑的数值膨胀，海量的局外养成也意味着卡关是不可能的，只是时间问题而已。 音乐美术方面没什么亮点，音乐不难听，画风不丑，也谈不上优秀。 总的来说这个游戏优点和缺点都是非常明显的。优点在于它几乎没有什么操作门槛，也很少需要复杂决策，所有设计都在服务同一件事——让屏幕尽快被弹射的球、跳动的数字和爆炸的特效填满。它玩起来也很方便，随时随地点开即玩，控制人物捡捡经验选选升级轻轻松松又过一关。随着游玩时间增加，怪物的数值和局外养成的数值同步成长，你会看到更加密密麻麻的数字和更夸张的攻击特效，这就是球比伦战记的快乐所在。 与此同时，缺点跟优点一样显而易见，极低的门槛和极低的操作上限，注定意味着你的决策和操作几乎不会对每局游戏产生任何影响。换句话说，即使你的手指在键盘上搓冒烟了也不能打出什么精彩的操作或者助你反败为胜。每一局虽然是从头开始，但由于局外成长的过强会导致新鲜感褪去之后你会发现这游戏你能不能赢跟你一点关系都没有，只要局外数值堆得够高闭着眼睛都能赢。局外养成带来的稳定正反馈，逐渐替代了玩家对机制的理解和操作的提升。最后决定你能否通关的，不是这一局打得怎么样，而是上一百局刷了多久。这也是我不太喜欢诸如吸血鬼幸存者这类靠局外养成推动游戏的肉鸽，我私以为这种设计虽然通过直接的数值提升给了玩家稳定的正反馈，但也毁掉了肉鸽的本质和纯粹性。 [h1]《球比伦战记》最大的乐趣来自爽感，而最大的缺点也恰恰来自这种爽感。[/h1]

BALL x PIT is a very enjoyable little game that combines Arkanoid style gameplay with elements inspired by Vampire Survivors, creating a surprisingly addictive experience. The main idea is simple. Bounce, destroy enemies, collect upgrades, and gradually become stronger. However, the real highlight is the ability to combine and upgrade balls, creating completely wild combinations that can turn your build into an unstoppable machine. Some of these combinations become so powerful that they almost feel like they are breaking the game, and that's part of the fun. The combination of automatic progression, different abilities, and constant upgrades creates a gameplay loop that is hard to put down. Every run feels rewarding, and there is always a reason to try "just one more time" to unlock new upgrades or discover another crazy build. The game doesn't reinvent the wheel, but it perfectly understands what makes this type of game fun. Every run feels rewarding, and there is always a reason to try "just one more time" to unlock new upgrades or improve your build. Pros: + Very addictive gameplay loop + Great combination of Arkanoid and Vampire Survivors mechanics + Crazy builds that can become hilariously overpowered + Simple but satisfying gameplay + Perfect for short gaming sessions Cons: - Gameplay can become repetitive after longer sessions - Simple concept may not appeal to everyone

im at a point in my life where i dont have the time to play games where you must pay full attention. its much easier to pick up a roguelike that you can drop and get into at any moment rather than a story heavy game or one thats "control heavy". i.e, its super easy to work on something else or eat or watch something while playing a roguelike. but at the same time, because so many roguelikes have come out in recent years i feel like im wasting my time. grinding out a bunch of characters, unlocking stuff thats supposed to keep you hooked but really just ends up with you backtracking to early levels, gameplay differences that are small but enough to make you think of cool builds but not actually get them due to randomization, and finally, huge difficulty spikes that encourage further grinding rather than experimenting with what you already have. additionally, where other game synergies feel more thoughtful, some of these completely remove the identity of the previous items (evolutions) or tend to forget about/downright nerf one of the two fusion components(fusion with things like dark & ghost completely nullify ghost, so why ever try a combo you'd think might be beneficial?) imo, these are the biggest issues with this game. not because the game itself is bad, but because the genre is so tired and this game doesnt improve anything i'm already tired of. if this was sent back 5 or 10 years, i wouldnt think about these issues. in the present, if i had to tell you to play one single roguelike, i might say to play this one at the very least. i just cant help but feel like im wasting my time playing this game, and then stuff like the aforementioned iffy fusions discourages me further to invest. i know the purpose of roguelikes is to adapt and overcome, but im tired of getting shafted by terrible rolls, fusions that dont work, and difficulty spikes that make it hard to want to continue. with the random stats you get from level up the RNG is furthered, some builds will be way stronger one run than another. i realize this is for variety, but it isnt really fun. finally, there are some items that will straight up kill you if you take them, be it by accident or because there are no good options on said roll. i.e, theres items that make your balls go through enemies, which early on will almost always instantly end your run. for the good, its cheap. its another roguelike so it'll be super easy to get into. the art&graphics are very unique and nice(but hitboxes are kinda hard to judge due to them sometimes), its probably super easy to run(but gets my pc hot for some reason where other games do not), the ball thing is satisfying and perfect for tiktok/youtube background footage. pretty much everything you'd want from a cheap game. but in my 10 hours, despite it being appealing on the surface, i absolutely do not want to keep playing it. this is the only roguelike i've ever played a run of and immediately wanted to get off. games like vampire survivors hook you and make you want to keep playing. dont know why that is, but its just how i feel.

Superficially you will have the impression that this is a rogue-lite action game, but that's almost more thematic than it is the core of the game. The game this most reminds me of is [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1289810/Siralim_Ultimate/]Siralim Ultimate[/url]. Neither game offers much skill expression through gameplay, with the actual gameplay part of the game being very light. In both cases the real core of the game is theory crafting, and the meta progression elements. Ball x Pit is more about the unlocks, incremental systems, the grind, and your build. The actual brick-breaking is very light, and has little variance beyond the visual. Placing on the leaderboards is mostly a question of how much time you are willing to invest on an endless run, or on furthering your meta progression. It's still a good time though. My only complaints would be that dealing with popups becomes annoying in a long endless run, and sometimes leaderboard scores don't submit.

Ah, BALL x PIT.. Yet another, overrated roguelite.. It's a shame, because it's one I really wanted to like at that too, but reality quickly got that idea out of my head. The biggest issue? The village/town. It's just a dumb resource grind that's not even fun, unless you are have a predisposition to enjoy tireless grind, combined with just as tiresome, Tetris style village/town building - It's alll about optimization, not fun, or getting your place to look neat in any way, shape or form. I seen a lot of praise for this part of the game, people even calling it better and more enjoyable than the actual game itself, but again, those opinions and reviews come from people who are already into this kind of stuff or are predisposed to potentially enjoy it. I will give it that the game has a very decent level variety and a decent amount of challenge for an average person or a casual player - It's fun, seeing the core gameplay loop kept intact, without being changed too much just for the sake of it, like some other games in roguelite & roguelike genres tend to do. Enemies that stack on top of each other, some shooting lasers, traps that you need to avoid or they will slow you down or you will slip on them in the ice and sand levels, music that's nice, and just as tiring as it may be to try and go for new ball evolutions, and just as it may be disappointing to find out that the evolution you just discovered is completely different from what you imagined, exploring all of those possibilities is also fun, and discovering it all, at least up until you have only a few evolutions left to discover, by which point it turns into a chore of experimentation. Still.. A very solid gameplay loop, that's just sadly locked away behind grind of village/town building, so that the player has to mess around with stuff they might not enjoy to improve their actual runs and chances of winning them. But hey, from more positives, the bosses are creative too - Yeah, they are bullet hell-ish sometimes, but it's not really all that bad if you just pay attention to your moves, and the enemies being damage sponges is actually fun here, because that's what the game is about, in the sense of, watch tons of bigger and smaller balls bounce off of enemies tens or hundreds of times until they die in a satisfying manner that makes you feel good about you beating them. Would I recommend BALL x PIT though? On one hand.. It depends if you enjoy resource management and village/town building aspects in your games, maybe Tetris style gameplay too where you just have to put shapes together and pray it works, but on the other hand, from my personal experience, I would say to avoid this one, even if the main game itself is solid. Had this been stripped of the whole "rebuild this town/village/city" aspect, I would have had kept playing it and recommended it, but as it stands, I can't recommend a game that taints my experience of it.
